title: Hawara Egyptian Labyrinth — Research and Timeline Pack

site.name: Hawara Pyramid and Labyrinth precinct
site.dating_note: 19th century BCE; exact construction phases vary by chronology
site.area_note: ~120 × 300 m cult precinct cited by University of Leeds, not an excavated room-by-room plan

critical_model_rules: The Labyrinth is a distinct Faiyum site separate from Giza.
Separate actual monumental remains from historically reconstructed rooms.
The 3,000 rooms and 1,500 underground rooms are Herodotus reports, not measured data.
A scan amplitude/contrast anomaly is not a chamber, and modeled survey depths are not proven room floors.
Do not display proprietary satellite claims as confirmed structure geometry.
Do not imply archaeological discoveries in 2010 or 2025 mean the buildings came into existence in those years.
No publicly validated exact labyrinth room plan; do not interpolate a walkable true interior from scans.
Digital reconstructions need creators rights/permissions prior to embedding assets.
Water depth values depend on survey year, surface elevation and method.

scans.title: Groundwater isotope and chemistry investigation
scans.observation: Canal-related saline water ingress and salt damage

scans.title: NRIAG Hawara geophysics report
scans.observation: The available April report chiefly documents background, goals and proposed techniques
scans.limit: Do not conflate its list of proposed methods with confirmed executed scans or validated chambers

scans.title: VLF-EM and vertical electrical sounding
scans.extent: 100 × 140 m south of pyramid, 2 m spacing
scans.observation: Linear and square conductivity anomalies; published pseudosections at ~4 and 8 m plus 3, 5, 12 m slices
scans.limit: Anomalies could also reflect geology, water or other remains; no excavated/validated 3D floorplan

scans.title: TEM and GEM hydrological survey
scans.extent: Temple precinct, pyramid and eastern cultivated lands
scans.observation: Groundwater generally ~2–7 m below ground in study; irrigation supplies water
scans.limit: Conductivity maps do not count rooms, artifacts or depth of entire labyrinth

scans.title: Hawara GPR geological study
scans.observation: Radar sections to ~20 m, possible wall-like features and groundwater pathways
scans.limit: Author explicitly states findings do not establish Herodotus’s labyrinth

scans.title: GeoScan/Boulter satellite imagery interpretation
scans.observation: Advocacy images depict separate flooded and dry levels
scans.limit: No independent validation, survey coordinates, depth calibration or raw method found

scans.title: Merlin Burrows / Akers satellite claims
scans.observation: Advocates claim deep chambers, boats and metallic item
scans.limit: No reproducible peer-reviewed floor plan, excavated confirmation, or publicly validated deep-penetration measurement

scans.title: Virtual Hawara terrestrial laser scan and GIS
scans.observation: Georeferenced 3D point cloud of surface conditions and modeled reconstruction
scans.limit: Reconstructions of vanished rooms are interpretations, not scans of intact underground labyrinth

scans.title: Carlotto ALOS PALSAR and Sentinel-1 SAR analysis
scans.extent: Either side of modern canal, south of pyramid
scans.observation: Unusual radar/optical discrepancies interpreted as possibly related to subsurface features
scans.limit: Indirect hypothesis; no independently verified deep-tunnel tomography or chamber count; satellite SAR not interchangeable with conventional on-site GPR

scans.title: Resumed excavation
scans.limit: No verified publication supplied with a mapped labyrinth interior or secure context for large wall claim

events.title: Faiyum before the Labyrinth
events.summary: Middle Kingdom rulers intensify projects in the Faiyum; the Hawara site belongs to this regional landscape.
events.visualization: Context map showing Nile-Faiyum corridor and settlements; do not assign precise canal works to one ruler.

events.title: Amenemhat III takes the throne
events.summary: The ruler associated with Hawara is Amenemhat III of Dynasty 12. Regnal chronologies differ.
events.visualization: Show dynasty and ruler card.

events.title: The earlier Dahshur pyramid
events.summary: Amenemhat III also built the Black Pyramid at Dahshur, likely preceding the Hawara complex. Reasons for shifting focus require careful wording.
events.visualization: Optional off-site comparison inset, not a building at Hawara.

events.title: Building begins at Hawara
events.summary: A geophysical paper cites an estimated beginning around Amenemhat III regnal year 15; do not present 1840 BCE as a documented exact date.
events.visualization: Fade in pyramid footprint and quarry/construction zone.

events.title: The cult temple complex rises
events.summary: The large temple south of the pyramid, often identified with the Labyrinth, likely dates to the latter part of Amenemhat III reign. Its detailed plan remains unknown.
events.visualization: Build a simplified 120×300 m conceptual mass with alternate-plan toggle and visible speculative label.

events.title: Royal burial and cult
events.summary: Mudbrick pyramid with stone passages and burial chamber, adjoining royal cult zone; details of exact interment and rituals should not be animated as known eyewitness scenes.
events.visualization: Show confirmed pyramid and idealized casing plus clearly flagged hypothetical ritual activity.

events.title: The cemetery around Hawara
events.summary: The site includes Late Middle Kingdom graves and later reuse, not only the royal complex.
events.visualization: Cemetery markers, dated by excavation contexts rather than interpolated exact years.

events.title: The memory of Amenemhat III
events.summary: The royal cult and local traditions survived long after original construction; this marker represents a long process, not a single event.
events.visualization: Temple activity slider shown with uncertain intensity.

events.title: Herodotus visits the Labyrinth
events.summary: Herodotus described twelve courts and reported 3,000 rooms, saying he saw the upper level but not the underground chambers.
events.visualization: Offer 12-court textual overlay; alleged underground 1,500 rooms in reported-only layer.

events.title: Diodorus repeats the wonder
events.summary: Diodorus credits the complex to a king named Mares/Mendes and preserves a tradition linking it to the Cretan labyrinth. Attribution differs from archaeological identification.
events.visualization: Compare ancient authors; no asserted architectural changes.

events.title: Strabo describes courtyards and immense stone roofs
events.summary: Strabo describes courts, winding corridors, monolithic pillars and roof stones beside the royal pyramid. His counts differ from Herodotus.
events.visualization: Switch from Herodotus narrative plan to Strabo plan with annotated contradictions.

events.title: Building stone removed and re-used
events.summary: During Ptolemaic and Roman periods the complex was extensively quarried and reused. Do not impose a single date for its disappearance.
events.visualization: Progressively reduce idealized temple to fragmented foundation beds.

events.title: Fayum mummy portraits
events.summary: Hawara became an important Roman-period cemetery; some burials bore painted mummy portraits later recovered by Petrie.
events.visualization: Reveal burial landscape and museum-linked objects; distinguish grave goods from temple chambers.

events.title: French expedition maps Hawara
events.summary: French-era surveyors documented the pyramid and neighbouring remains; later published descriptions sometimes misidentified visible structures.
events.visualization: Historical map overlay, clearly marked as interpretation.

events.title: Lepsius excavates and maps
events.summary: The Prussian expedition investigated structures near the pyramid, but some masonry Lepsius associated with the original complex was later reassigned to Roman occupation.
events.visualization: Toggle Lepsius historical plan versus modern archaeological assessment.

events.title: Petrie begins systematic excavation
events.summary: Flinders Petrie investigates pyramid, temple platform and cemeteries; first campaigns run 1888–1889.
events.visualization: Excavation trenches and published plan overlay.

events.title: Petrie documents the pyramid interior
events.summary: Excavation helps define Hawara pyramid internal architecture while surviving temple fabric remains limited.
events.visualization: Show documented pyramid passages separately from hypothetical labyrinth rooms.

events.title: Petrie returns to Hawara
events.summary: Petrie undertakes another season in 1910–1911. His proposed Labyrinth plan remained schematic and substantially reconstructed from ancient texts.
events.visualization: Show footprint from his publication; mark conjectural room positions.

events.title: Leuven survey relocates sculpture
events.summary: University of Leuven team locates two Middle Kingdom sculptures in western temple area. Peer-reviewed publication followed in 2002.
events.visualization: Plot sculpture-find zones with approximate localization.

events.title: Groundwater origin investigated
events.summary: Stable-isotope chemistry points to the Bahr Selah canal as a principal source of ingress; salt accumulation threatens the pyramid.
events.visualization: Groundwater layer, not rooms; use time-specific study values.

events.title: Electromagnetic prospecting at Hawara
events.summary: An NRIAG-linked survey gathers VLF-EM and resistivity data south of the pyramid. Detailed interpretations appear in 2010.
events.visualization: Show original scan grid; no revealed hallways.

events.title: VLF-EM survey reports patterned anomalies
events.summary: 75 VLF-EM profiles on a 100×140 m survey grid indicate elongated and rectilinear conductivity anomalies; modeled slices include depths of 4 m and 8 m. Authors describe a possible archaeological explanation, not verified rooms.
events.visualization: Display original geophysical figures with source links and separate interpretive traces.

events.title: TEM/GEM maps the water table
events.summary: 74 TEM stations and a GEM grid support groundwater levels varying around 2–7 m below surface in the study area. This is groundwater mapping, not an underground chamber map.
events.visualization: Hydrology contours with time-slice disclaimer.

events.title: Ground-penetrating radar identifies possible features
events.summary: GPR cross-sections extend to approximately 20 m in a conservation survey; some reflections may represent walls, but the author states this does not demonstrate Herodotus’s labyrinth.
events.visualization: Show actual cross-sections 653 and north-side N1 plus uncertain feature traces.

events.title: GeoScan satellite reconstruction publicized
events.summary: A claimed two-level flooded/unflooded model was publicized by project advocates; no accessible independent archaeological validation or raw-data workflow was identified.
events.visualization: Violet-only visual with provenance banner; do not use as surveyed mesh.

events.title: Merlin Burrows deep-structure claims
events.summary: Claims of deep halls, boats, and a large metal object depend on advocates’ accounts; no verifiable independent scans demonstrating these structures were located.
events.visualization: Claims layer off by default; no confirmed object geometry.

events.title: Virtual Hawara documents the site
events.summary: UK/Egypt university collaboration develops terrestrial laser survey, topographic GIS, and evidence-led digital reconstructions. A digital reconstruction is not direct observation of intact underground corridors.
events.visualization: Show site point-cloud/terrain as observed layer and color idealized buildings separately.

events.title: Spaceborne SAR hypothesis published
events.summary: Mark Carlotto argues radar differences from two satellite systems may reflect buried features south of Hawara; this is an indirect interpretation and does not map proven deep rooms.
events.visualization: Violet interpreted-anomaly footprints, linked to paper with methodology caveat.

events.title: Egyptian excavation resumes at Hawara
events.summary: Egyptian news dated 7 May 2026 reports the Supreme Council of Antiquities Fayoum mission excavating to identify labyrinth remains. Independent context for claimed new megalithic wall was not located.
events.visualization: Show active research marker; do not add revealed deep chambers or a validated wall plan.
